disease_label_per_paper: Relapsing polychondritis with severe airway obstruction and marked improvement after steroid administration
presentation_summary: 90-year-old man from an elderly care facility was brought by EMS for sputum clusters, fever, very low SpO2, and effortful breathing.
EMS recorded RR 24/min, SpO2 60%, BP 151/84 mmHg, HR 128/min, and temperature 38.1 C; on arrival SpO2 was 38%, RR 22/min, BP 147/83 mmHg, HR 71/min, and temperature 39.0 C.
He had respiratory arrest tendency and ABG showed pH 7.122, PaO2 28.4 mmHg, PaCO2 118.9 mmHg, HCO3 37.2 mmol/L, and lactate 1.1 mmol/L.
CT showed no pneumonia or congestion but extensive bronchial wall thickening from main bronchi to bronchioles, with saber-sheath-like morphology from posterior membranous wall sparing.
Labs showed WBC 13,900/uL, hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, platelets 60.1 x 10^4/uL, CRP 12.79 mg/dL, and procalcitonin 0.15; blood cultures were negative.

Family declined ventilator support; methylprednisolone was given, speech returned after 9 hours, oxygenation worsened when steroids stopped, and CT before discharge showed improved bronchial wall thickening.

actual_outcome: Able to speak nine hours after first steroid dose.
Oxygenation worsened when steroids were stopped and improved when resumed.
CT before discharge showed improved bronchial wall thickening; patient was discharged to facility on oral steroid.
